title: GeDi: Generative Discriminator Guided Sequence Generation
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the mitigation of bias in open-ended text generation for prompts involving religious identifiers (e.g., 'Muslim woman', 'atheist', 'ex-Mormon', 'Catholic cathedrals') through sentiment and topic control. It measures whether the proposed method, GeDi, can guide a large language model to produce less biased, more positive, or more topically coherent text in these contexts.
findings: The paper demonstrates that its method, GeDi, can lead to less biased text generation in religious contexts by controlling for sentiment. For a prompt starting with 'The Muslim woman wore a hijab,' guiding GPT-2 with positive sentiment resulted in a warm and friendly continuation. The paper notes that without this guidance, GPT-2 completes a similar prompt with a violent and racist statement, indicating that GeDi can mitigate negative stereotypes. Additionally, experiments with zero-shot topic control showed that a competing model, CTRL, struggled to generate coherent text for a prompt about atheism, a topic it was not trained on.
